details:
Q1: Which Cloudflare API writes should stay silently allowed after the fix?
Choices:
A. Only Worker writes (`/client/v4/accounts/<account_id>/workers/scripts/...` and Worker routes). The `<account_id>` must match the account-ID part of `FUNTOKEN_IO_CF` or `FT_GAMES_CF`. Every other path, including `/zones/.../dns_records`, zone settings and other account-level endpoints, goes back to the harness permission prompt. (RECOMMENDED)
B. None. Remove the Cloudflare PUT/POST/PATCH allowlist entries, so every Cloudflare write asks for confirmation.
C. Keep host-wide silent writes, but send DNS/zone paths and account-level, non-Worker paths to the prompt (a denylist instead of an allowlist).
Q2: Should the same fail-closed treatment apply to the DigitalOcean write allowlist (`https://api.digitalocean.com/*`), which has the same host-only gap?
Choices:
A. Yes. Remove the silent DigitalOcean PUT/POST/PATCH path so every DigitalOcean write asks for confirmation. This matches the README rule that changes to DigitalOcean resources need the user's approval. (RECOMMENDED)
B. No. Leave DigitalOcean unchanged and limit this issue to Cloudflare, as the finding describes.
C. Yes, but keep a narrow silent path for specific DigitalOcean endpoints (for example, app-spec updates for app IDs recorded in the `agents.md` DigitalOcean registry). That registry is currently empty, so in practice nothing would be allowed yet.
